answer: <think>The question asks whether nutmeg liver results from right-sided or left-sided heart failure. Nutmeg liver is a term used to describe the gross appearance of the liver when there is chronic passive congestion. Chronic passive congestion of the liver most frequently occurs when there is increased pressure in the hepatic veins, which drain into the inferior vena cava. This is most commonly due to right-sided heart failure, since the right ventricle is responsible for pumping blood to the lungs, and its failure leads to backing up of blood in the systemic circulation—including the hepatic veins.
